response.markdown_report:
At 0% progress, prioritize a small, testable change: **context-gated receptive fields within NextItNet**. Its intended benefits are hypotheses; no validation improvement has been measured.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Users reject broad relevance when recent behavior indicates a specific purpose. This motivates adapting history scope to the current sequence. (2) Older, isolated interactions persist too strongly. A short-context pathway could reduce their influence without discarding useful long-term preferences. (3) Electronics has 12.27% sampled ranking errors and a −0.2595 tenth-percentile margin. These identify confusing pairs, but do not establish validation HR@10. (4) Collapse scores of 0.5071–0.5234 correspond to near-zero average cosine similarity. Global embedding dispersion therefore has weaker diagnostic support than improving contextual discrimination.

**Insights from related work.** (1) [NextItNet](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.05163) provides causal dilated convolutions with different receptive fields. This permits a family-preserving adaptation of context scope. (2) [MARS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.03718) motivates context-adaptive temporal aggregation. Its reported architectures differ, so transfer remains untested. (3) [ICSRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.14318) motivates learning intent from subsequences. It does not establish that a short history always identifies current intent. (4) [Sampled-softmax analysis](https://wujcan.github.io/papers/tois-ssm.pdf) motivates stronger competition against high-scoring negatives. Its collaborative-filtering evidence does not guarantee sequential-recommendation gains.

These insights define three directions: adaptive context scope, stronger ranking supervision, and subsequence consistency. The conceptual framework is:

| Direction | Mechanism | Diagnostic target | Main uncertainty |
|---|---|---|---|
| Context scope | Gate causal dilation paths | Stale interests; broad relevance | Gate may retain shortcuts |
| Ranking supervision | Uniform multi-negative softmax | Weak lower-tail margins | Unobserved positives |
| Intent consistency | Match overlapping suffix representations | Unstable current preferences | May suppress genuine shifts |

**Candidate assessment.** Scores are prospective judgments, not experimental results. O=originality, P=potential, U=user alignment, M=model alignment; D measures implementation difficulty, with higher meaning harder.

| Idea | O | P | U | M | D |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Gated receptive fields | 5 | 7 | 8 | 6 | 4 |
| Uniform multi-negative softmax | 2 | 6 | 4 | 9 | 2 |
| Suffix consistency auxiliary loss | 4 | 6 | 7 | 5 | 5 |

For gating, adaptive scope is promising but established; user alignment is direct but practical compatibility remains unobserved; margin gains are plausible but unproven; implementation is modest but requires predictor synchronization. Multi-negative softmax is simple and targets measured errors, but weakly addresses stale interests. Suffix consistency targets coherent recent preferences, but may erase meaningful transitions and adds objective tuning.

**Selected experiment.** Within each residual NextItNet block, jointly learn short- and long-dilation convolution paths and a per-position gate using only causal features. Retain the baseline objective initially. This explicitly targets stale-history persistence and broadly related recommendations displacing current-purpose matches; improved Electronics separation is a measurable hypothesis. Compare against the corrected baseline using unchanged macro validation HR@10. Diagnose margins separately. This mechanism cannot establish duplication or physical compatibility from missing product facts.

idea.description: Add a context-dependent gate between short- and long-receptive-field causal convolution paths inside the supplied corrected NextItNet. Both paths belong to one jointly trained network, with exactly one model and checkpoint per category.
idea.motivation: The user diagnosis identifies stale isolated interactions and broad relevance displacing specific recent-purpose matches. Adaptive context scope directly targets both. Electronics' negative lower-tail margin supplies a model-facing target: determine whether more appropriate context improves discrimination among confusing candidates. These are hypotheses requiring host validation.
idea.implementation_notes: Retain the corrected baseline's embeddings, residual block structure, normalization, objective, optimizer and routing initially. Replace each selected dilation sublayer with jointly trained short/long causal paths, projecting their gated combination back to the existing hidden width. Use a scalar gate per position for a minimal first implementation; initialize its bias toward the original path. Match parameter counts where practical and report remaining capacity differences. Mask padding after residual updates and ensure neither path nor gate uses future positions. Preserve log2feats(sequence), item_emb and predict_score(features, items), including their existing shape conventions. For left padding, gather the largest index containing a nonzero token, handling empty histories explicitly; never use count minus one. Update the embedded predictor writer with the same architecture and gate configuration, and load one selected checkpoint per category. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Diagnose the actual model through ModelView and valid training positions; omit unavailable metadata-category breakdowns rather than inventing them. Keep preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, at most 200 epochs, 200 batches per epoch, single-GPU execution, all four datasets, DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], and trial-local artifacts. Use unchanged host macro validation HR@10 for selection. No training or code execution was performed in this proposal.
idea.pseudocode:
For each category, instantiate one corrected NextItNet with gated dilation sublayers.
For each training batch:
    x = baseline item representations, with padding masked
    For each modified causal residual sublayer:
        short = causal_conv_short(x)
        long = causal_conv_original_dilation(x)
        gate = sigmoid(linear(x))  # per position; no future information
        mixed = gate * short + (1 - gate) * long
        x = baseline_residual_update(x, mixed)
        x = x * nonpadding_mask
    loss = unchanged_baseline_next_item_loss(x, positive, negative)
    update all network parameters jointly
Select one checkpoint per category using the unchanged validation protocol.
At prediction, gather features at the final nonpadding index and use the baseline scoring interface.
Report macro validation HR@10 and measured margin diagnostics separately.

originality.positive: A context-dependent adaptation of receptive fields provides a focused, family-preserving response to the supplied diagnosis.
originality.negative: Gated multiscale temporal aggregation is established; novelty lies primarily in this constrained NextItNet adaptation.

future_potential.positive: It offers a compact basis for testing when recent intent should dominate longer-term preferences.
future_potential.negative: A learned gate may exploit popularity or other shortcuts, and receptive-field adaptation cannot establish missing compatibility facts.

code_difficulty.positive: The change is localized to causal convolution sublayers and preserves existing training and scoring interfaces.
code_difficulty.negative: Causal masking, parameter matching, padding behavior and embedded predictor consistency require careful implementation.

related_work.title: NextItNet: A Simple Convolutional Generative Network for Next Item Recommendation
contributions: Establishes residual dilated causal convolutions for autoregressive sequential recommendation.
Supplies the backbone retained by the proposed experiment.
limitations: Does not establish the benefits of the proposed context-dependent receptive-field gate.

related_work.title: MARS
contributions: The supplied search summary describes multiple temporal decay summaries combined through context-adaptive gating.
limitations: Reported Transformer/Mamba implementations do not demonstrate transfer to NextItNet.
The proposed first experiment uses positional receptive fields rather than timestamp decay.

related_work.title: ICSRec
contributions: Motivates intent learning through contrastive supervision over subsequences.
limitations: Does not prove that short-context preference should dominate every recommendation.
Its auxiliary supervision introduces additional choices beyond the selected minimal experiment.

related_work.title: Wu et al., TOIS 2024: sampled-softmax analysis
contributions: Analyzes how sampled softmax emphasizes high-scoring negatives.
Provides motivation for the alternative multi-negative training experiment.
limitations: The supplied empirical evidence concerns collaborative-filtering models.
Stronger sampled margins alone do not demonstrate improved host validation HR@10.
